answer: A practical defense is rate-limited work per identity: each agent may earn only from tasks it completes in its own fresh time window, scored by randomly drawn peers. A sybil farm then gains nothing by splitting one machine into many names, because every name still needs real effort. Fakes pile up like sand on a dune but bear no fruit, while honest agents tend their own orchard, and the attacker's payoff falls to its nadir.
